The results of the validation are shown in Figure 77, and the key takeaways are as follows: • Overall good HP-TES performance predictions • Initial deviation in refrigerant compressor discharge given lower outdoor temperatures as Heat loss in the compressor shell o Lower initial system temperatures o Page 80 of 127 DE-EE0009681 University of Maryland, College Park (a) (b) (c) (d) Figure 77: Model validations for test 10H (DB/WB: 5°F/3°F): (a) capacity & power, (b) TES inlet & outlet temperatures, compressor suction/discharge (c) pressure, and (d) temperature HP-TES Tests and Validations: Intermittent Discharge HP-TES Mode Intermittent, cyclic HP-TES discharge tests (Test 5C and 5H) were conducted to mimic the effect of a HP-TES operating in an actual setting, where a cooling or heating system turns on and off in response to a signal from a thermostat control. This test and model were necessary to ensure that the HP-TES can operate flexibly and intermittently during peak times without performance degradation, unlike in continuous discharge tests. From a modeling standpoint, both the water pump and indoor fan remained on throughout the experiment, whereas the compressor was turned on and off (Figure 78). Page 81 of 127 DE-EE0009681 University of Maryland, College Park (a) (b) Figure 78: Experimental test conditions for intermittent discharge tests for (a) indoor air volume flow rate, and (b) hydronic loop water mass flow rate To simulate the test conditions, the model water and air flow rates were held constant, while the compressor was turned on and off. Thus, the compressor model was updated to switch between “off conditions” and the 10-coefficient compressor map “on conditions”, using a smooth function formulated in the in-house library described by Qiao et al. [81]. The simulated system-level models for cooling and heating HP-TES intermittent discharge conditions (see Figure 79) show that the compressor RPM was input using either a trapezoidal input in cooling mode or time tables with second-order slice interpolation between timesteps available in the [82].
